title: Web app on a private virtual machine behind an Application Gateway
summary: Runs your application on a virtual machine that has only a private address. Users reach it through an Application Gateway, which is the only part with a public address. Network security groups limit traffic so that only the gateway can reach the server.
match_phrases: deploy my app on a server
host a web app on a virtual machine
run my website on a vm

facts.statement: Resources in a resource group should share the same lifecycle. Deleting a resource group deletes every resource in it.
Each virtual network is isolated from other virtual networks, so its traffic is not reachable by other Azure customers.
Microsoft recommends associating network security groups with subnets rather than with individual network interfaces where possible.
Security rule priority is a number from 100 to 4096. Lower numbers are processed first. Priority must be unique within the inbound rules and within the outbound rules.
Every network security group has default rules, including AllowVNetInBound at 65000, AllowAzureLoadBalancerInBound at 65001 and DenyAllInbound at 65500. Custom rules are processed before them.
Application Gateway requires a dedicated subnet. Other resources such as virtual machines or private endpoints cannot share it.
A /24 subnet is recommended for Application Gateway v2 so autoscaling has room for more instances.
For Application Gateway v2 without network isolation, the gateway subnet must allow inbound TCP 65200 to 65535 from the GatewayManager service tag to any destination.
Inbound traffic from the AzureLoadBalancer service tag must be allowed on the gateway subnet and must not be overridden by a manual deny rule.
Outbound internet connectivity from the gateway subnet must not be blocked.
Application Gateway v2 supports Standard SKU public IP addresses that are static only.
Basic SKU public IP addresses were retired on 30 September 2025.
The v2 SKU types include Standard_v2 and WAF_v2.
Managed disks, including the OS disk, are encrypted at rest by default with platform managed keys, and this cannot be disabled.
Default server side encryption does not cover temp disks or disk caches. Encryption at host adds encryption for those.
Azure has built-in roles including Reader, Virtual Machine User Login and Virtual Machine Administrator Login.

explanation.what: A resource group is a folder for Azure resources.
explanation.why: Everything for this app lives together, so you can manage, secure and remove it as one unit. Deleting the group deletes everything in it.

explanation.what: A virtual network is your own private network inside Azure.
explanation.why: It gives the server a private address. It is isolated from other customers' networks.

explanation.what: A network security group is a set of firewall rules.
explanation.why: This one protects the gateway subnet. It lets users reach the gateway on its listener port and allows the Azure management traffic the gateway needs to work.

explanation.what: A network security group is a set of firewall rules.
explanation.why: This one protects the server subnet. Only the gateway may reach the server, and traffic from the internet is denied.

explanation.what: A subnet is a section of the virtual network.
explanation.why: Application Gateway needs a subnet of its own. A /24 is recommended so it can scale out.

explanation.what: A subnet is a section of the virtual network.
explanation.why: This one holds the server on a private address range, with its own firewall rules.

explanation.what: A public IP address is an address on the internet.
explanation.why: The gateway needs one so users can reach your app. The server never gets one. Application Gateway v2 requires a Standard, static address.

explanation.what: Application Gateway is a web traffic load balancer that receives user requests.
explanation.why: It is the only public entry point and forwards requests to your private server. The WAF_v2 type adds a web application firewall.

explanation.what: A virtual machine is a server in Azure that runs your application.
explanation.why: It has only a private address and is reachable only through the gateway. Its disks are encrypted at rest by default.

explanation.what: A role assignment gives a group permission on a set of resources.
explanation.why: Your operators get only the access they need, following least privilege.

nsg_rules.name: allow-https-listener
nsg_rules.description: Users reach the gateway listener over HTTPS

nsg_rules.name: allow-gateway-manager
nsg_rules.description: Azure infrastructure traffic required by Application Gateway v2

nsg_rules.name: allow-https-from-gateway
nsg_rules.description: Only the gateway subnet may reach the server, over HTTPS

nsg_rules.name: deny-internet-inbound
nsg_rules.description: Deny anything else from the internet

questions.text: Do you already have a Microsoft Entra tenant for your organisation?
questions.why: Everything in Azure lives under a tenant. If you need a new one, it is created outside this tool first.

options.label: No, I need to create one

questions.text: Should this go into an existing Azure subscription, or a new one?
questions.why: A subscription holds the resources and receives the bill.

questions.text: Which Azure region should host the app?
questions.why: Pick one close to your users. Not every service or size is offered in every region, so the region is checked before code is generated.

questions.text: Which operating system does your app need?
questions.why: This decides the server image and how administrators sign in.

questions.text: Which port does your app listen on inside the server?
questions.why: The gateway forwards traffic to this port. HTTPS keeps traffic encrypted all the way to the server.

questions.text: Do you want a web application firewall on the gateway?
questions.why: WAF_v2 inspects requests and blocks common web attacks. Standard_v2 does not.

questions.text: Which private address range should the network use?
questions.why: It must not overlap with networks you may connect later, such as your office.

questions.text: Which groups of people need access to these resources?
questions.why: Access is given to groups, not individuals. Real names stay on your machine and are replaced by placeholders before anything is sent to the AI.

questions.text: What should the people who run this be able to do?
questions.why: Least privilege: give only the access the job needs.

known_gaps: Logging and monitoring resources are not modelled yet. The project guardrails require them, so they must be added before Slice 2 generates code.
The TLS certificate for the HTTPS listener is not modelled yet.
An administrator access path to the private server, such as Azure Bastion, is not modelled yet.
Region availability of each service and size is not checked yet. It will come from Azure APIs, not from the AI.
Encryption at host for temp disks is not enabled yet. Its prerequisites need to be checked first.
Private only Application Gateway deployments (network isolation) are not covered.
